title: How break leveling works
text: user-confirmed break window [b_start, b_end], dm_level_breaks() four things: Reference lookup. Take nearest non-NA value b_start (v1) b_end (v2), bounded within growth_window_days endpoint. Bounding matters: break endpoints usually sit gap edges, unbounded search grab reference across unrelated sensor gap apply wrong offset. -window reference exists either side, -gap span deleted, shift skipped, warning names series break. Delete -gap span (value <- NA inside window). Growth extrapolation. Estimate pre-break growth rate (µm/day) growth_window_days break (growth_method: daily median regression default), cap max_slope_day, multiply growing-season seconds inside gap – dormant time contributes growth. Cap total max_growth_total. Shift. Add adj = v1 - v2 + g_est everything b_end. adj non-finite (endpoint NA cell), shift skipped post-break data preserved un-levelled, warning – never silently nulled. Multiple breaks per series applied chronological order, shifts accumulate.

title: How break leveling works
text: post-break segment drops ~35 µm (injected step) minus small growth extrapolated 4-hour window.
code: d <- subset(dendro_sample, series == "SYN_Pa002")  levelled <- dm_level_breaks(   d, brks = list(SYN_Pa002 = list(     c("2022-06-15 10:00:00", "2022-06-15 14:00:00")))) #> dm_level_breaks [breaks]: 1 break(s) across 1 series... #>   |                                                          |                                                  |   0%  |                                                          |==================================================| 100% #>   plot(d$ts, d$value, type = "l", col = "grey60",      xlab = "", ylab = "stem radius (µm)") lines(levelled$ts, levelled$value, col = "firebrick") legend("topleft", c("raw", "levelled"), col = c("grey60", "firebrick"),        lty = 1, bty = "n")

title: How break leveling works
text: dm_clean_series() runs full sequence; step also callable alone: Note: dm_clean_series() runs erasure alignment single combined pass (one grouped sweep per series) behavior-stable reference – output pinned byte--byte original DendroMatic implementation package test suite.
code: d |>   dm_level_breaks(brks)  |>   # 1. remove sensor artefacts   dm_erase_dormancy()    |>   # 2. NA outside the growing season   dm_align_seasons()     |>   # 3. carry growth across winters   dm_rebase_zero()            # 4. floor each series at zero

title: How break leveling works
text: growth_window_days (default 14) controls reference search slope window. Short windows track fast growth phases better risk finding reference beside long gap; long windows smooth estimate can bridge differently-levelled data. break sits beside long gap see “-window reference” warning, widen window move break endpoints onto measured data.

code: d <- subset(dendro_sample, series == "SYN_Pa002") plot(d$ts, d$value, type = "l", xlab = "", ylab = "stem radius (µm)",      main = "SYN_Pa002, raw") abline(v = as.POSIXct("2022-06-15 12:00:00", tz = "UTC"), col = "red", lty = 2)

title: Getting started with dendromatic
text: dm_clean_series() applies, order: break leveling, dormancy erasure, season alignment, per-series zero re-basing. Break windows passed named list, one c(start, end) pair per break. rerun_proc_L2 = FALSE keeps vignette independent GitHub-‘treenetproc’ package; real pipeline leave TRUE TWD zero-growth columns recomputed.  step gone, dormancy period seasons erased, season two starts season one’s maximum, series minimum sits zero.
code: brks <- list(SYN_Pa002 = list(   c("2022-06-15 10:00:00", "2022-06-15 14:00:00") ))  cleaned <- dm_clean_series(   df            = dendro_sample,   brks          = brks,   grow_start_dm = "01-05",   # growing season: 1 May ...   grow_end_dm   = "31-10",   # ... to 31 October   rerun_proc_L2 = FALSE ) #> apply_breaks_and_shift [breaks]: 1 break(s) across 2 series... #>   |                                                          |                                                  |   0%  |                                                          |=========================                         |  50%  |                                                          |==================================================| 100% #>  #> apply_breaks_and_shift [dormancy/alignment]: 2 series... #>   |                                                          |                                                  |   0%  |                                                          |=========================                         |  50%  |                                                          |==================================================| 100% #> cd <- subset(cleaned, series == "SYN_Pa002") plot(cd$ts, cd$value, type = "l", xlab = "", ylab = "stem radius (µm)",      main = "SYN_Pa002, cleaned")

title: Getting started with dendromatic
text: Downstream water-relations work usually needs daily predawn minimum midday maximum tree water deficit (TWD). twd column (normally treenetproc L2 step), dm_pdmd_extrema() extracts local time:
code: ## toy TWD: running max minus value, per series cleaned$twd <- ave(cleaned$value, cleaned$series, FUN = function(v) {   m <- cummax(ifelse(is.na(v), -Inf, v)); ifelse(is.na(v), NA, m - v) }) pdmd <- dm_pdmd_extrema(cleaned, pd_start_hr = 3, pd_end_hr = 6,                         md_start_hr = 12, md_end_hr = 15, tz = "Etc/GMT-1") head(pdmd) #> # A tibble: 6 × 4 #>   series    date       pdtwd mdtwd #>   <chr>     <date>     <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 SYN_Fs001 2021-04-01    NA    NA #> 2 SYN_Fs001 2021-04-02    NA    NA #> 3 SYN_Fs001 2021-04-03    NA    NA #> 4 SYN_Fs001 2021-04-04    NA    NA #> 5 SYN_Fs001 2021-04-05    NA    NA #> 6 SYN_Fs001 2021-04-06    NA    NA
